newsitem.title: USA: Post-1997 Hong Kong economy faces boom - Tsang.
newsitem.headline: Post-1997 Hong Kong economy faces boom - Tsang.

text.p: Hong Kong's economy, which has had uninterrupted growth for 35 years, will surge even further once the territory reverts to Chinese rule, Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said.
"Once people wake up from the excessive pessimism, there will be a real boom in Hong Kong," Tsang told a meeting on the sidelines of the annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank.
He said Hong Kong's recent economic consolidation was a blessing in disguise, considering the struggle for recovery in Europe and economic overheating in the rest of Asia.
Inlfation has slowed, the property market completely recovered and the stock market is one of the leading performers of 1996.
The political outlook is also positive following the resolution of a number of issues, including on a final court of appeal and the decision to build a new Hong Kong airport.
He dismissed the argument that Hong Kong's economic growth would slow as it matures.

It was already a post-industrial economy, with more than 80 percent of its GDP attributable to services, and had the best conditions for staying the course of fast growth and fast transformation, Tsang said.
